0.1 This Indian

FOREWORD

Standard (Part III) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 27 October 1976, after the draft finalized by the Shipbuilding Sectional Committee had been approved by the Marine, Cargo Movement and Packaging Division Council. 0.2 The object of this standard is to specify the technical and scientific terms used in ship geometry, hydrostatic and hydrodynamic terms and to facilitate the exchange of information, particularly at international level, and the ease of understanding as regards to documents relating to naval architecture. 0.3 The terms are represented by symbols alphabetical order for ease of interpretation. which have been arranged in

0.4 No rules are laid down as to whether subscripts are to be shown by capital or lower case letters, although the letters shown in this standard are in the preferred style. 0.5 When required, the suffixes M and S should be introduced to distinguish between quantities referring to model and ship respectively. 0.6 This standard are : Part Part Part Part Part I II IV V VI Basic Ship is being issued in six parts. quantities geometry The other parts in the series

Sea keeping Manoeuvrability Strength and vibration 8 on `TerminoTowing Tank

0.7 While preparing this standard, current work by ISO/TC logy of profiles and hydrodynamic terms' and International Conference (ITTC) has also been considered.
